newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH TRUST IN HAVEL RISES TO POST-REVOLUTION LEVEL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH TRUST IN HAVEL RISES TO POST-REVOLUTION LEVEL.

text.p: Confidence in Czech President Vaclav Havel rose in December to match the level of trust citizens had in him soon after Prague's 1989 "Velvet Revolution", an opinion poll released on Thursday showed.
The survey by the state-funded research agency IVVM showed Havel had the trust of 84 percent of Czech citizens, up six percentage points from an IVVM survey in November.

The trust in Havel, who had radical cancer surgery to remove a tumour from his lungs on December 2, was similar to the level he enjoyed in his first two years in office after he helped lead the bloodless revolution over communsim in 1989.
Havel was released from hospital on the day after Christmas and is recuperating in his private villa in western Prague. He is expected to make a full recovery.

The poll showed 51 percent of Czech adults trust the three-party centre-right government, up five percentage points from November, and despite a wave of inter-party bickering ahead of December's approval of the 1997 balanced budget plan.
The early December survey was taken ahead of the resignation of Justice Minister Jan Kalovoda, the leader of the junior coaltion party the Civic Democratic Alliance.
Kalvoda quit his cabinet and parliament seat after admitting to falsely claiming to have a Doctor of Law degree.
Confidence in parliament, consistently the least trusted of Czech institutions, rose in December to 33 percent from 29 percent in November, the survey showed.
